boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Houston, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A paced, under-21-safe first-weekend circuit through central campus: get oriented, find practical spaces, try a low-stakes activity, and learn two visible Cougar traditions.

cards.title: Start at Student Center South
cards.subtitle: First stop: locate the campus hub
cards.notes: Use the building as an orientation anchor, then check the Information Center or posted events before choosing your next campus stop.
cards.short_summary: A central starting point for campus services, dining, and activities.
cards.evidence_claim: UH identifies its Student Centers as facilities supporting campus life; Student Center South is at 4455 University Drive.
cards.access_notes: Building hours listed by UH: Mon–Thu 7 a.m.–midnight; Fri–Sat 7 a.m.–1 a.m.; Sun 1 p.m.–midnight. Hours may change.

cards.title: Get a library bearings check
cards.subtitle: Second stop: M.D. Anderson Library
cards.notes: Walk through the main library and note its study-room, computer-lab, research-support, and course-reserve services for later in the term.
cards.short_summary: The main library is a practical place to learn early.
cards.evidence_claim: UH Libraries identifies M.D. Anderson Library as the main library on campus and lists study rooms, computer labs, and research support.
cards.access_notes: The library homepage lists daily hours; confirm the current schedule before going.

cards.title: Pause in Butler Plaza
cards.subtitle: Third stop: the plaza by the library
cards.notes: Take a short break outside M.D. Anderson Library, then use the plaza as a landmark for finding the surrounding academic buildings.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor campus landmark beside the main library.
cards.evidence_claim: UH describes Butler Plaza as the plaza bounded by the Ezekiel Cullen Building, M.D. Anderson Library, Technology Annex, and Philip G. Hoffman Hall.
cards.source_title: Freedom of Expression | University of Houston
cards.access_notes: Outdoor common areas are subject to campus operations and scheduled activities.

cards.title: See what’s showing at Blaffer
cards.subtitle: Fourth stop: contemporary art on campus
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition before you go, then give yourself time for one gallery loop rather than trying to rush every work.
cards.short_summary: A campus contemporary-art stop with no admission fee.
cards.evidence_claim: UH states that Blaffer Art Museum is the professional art museum on the main campus and is open to all without an admission fee.
cards.source_title: Blaffer Art Museum Student Service Fee Request Questionnaire
cards.access_notes: Verify current exhibition and visitor hours with the museum before visiting.

cards.title: Scope out Campus Recreation
cards.subtitle: Fifth stop: see the recreation center
cards.notes: Complete the required annual waiver before a first visit, then ask staff which open-recreation or group-fitness options fit your schedule.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation facility with fitness, sport, and wellness programs.
cards.evidence_claim: UH says the Campus Recreation and Wellness Center offers recreation programs including group fitness, intramural sports, outdoor adventure, and training.
cards.access_notes: UH requires an annual waiver before a first visit; check current facility hours and membership eligibility before arrival.

cards.title: Try the climbing wall
cards.subtitle: Sixth stop: a beginner-friendly activity
cards.notes: Sign in with Outdoor Adventure staff, borrow the required gear at the Welcome Desk, and choose a route that matches your comfort level.
cards.short_summary: A 53-foot indoor wall inside the Campus Recreation and Wellness Center.
cards.evidence_claim: UH describes the CRWC climbing wall as 53 feet tall; current CRWC members may climb with no additional cost, and no experience is required.
cards.source_title: Climbing Wall | University of Houston Outdoor Adventure
cards.access_notes: CRWC membership or sponsored-guest access is required. Sign in at the wall and complete required releases before climbing.

cards.title: Make an evening plan in the Games Room
cards.subtitle: Seventh stop: bowling, billiards, table tennis, or arcade
cards.notes: Check lane or table availability with the service counter, then pick one activity and follow the room’s equipment and safety directions.
cards.short_summary: A basement-level Student Center South recreation space.
cards.evidence_claim: UH says the Games Room includes a 12-lane bowling center, pool tables, table tennis, and a video arcade; open-play rates are posted.
cards.source_title: Student Centers Games Room | University of Houston
cards.access_notes: UH currently lists summer hours of 10 a.m.–8 p.m. Monday–Saturday and advises calling to confirm availability; posted open-play activities have charges.

cards.entity_name: Cougar Statues at the RAD Center
cards.title: Find the relocated Cougar statues
cards.subtitle: Eighth stop: a documented UH tradition
cards.notes: Visit the statues outside the RAD Center and, if you choose, take part in the paw-rubbing tradition before a game or exam.
cards.short_summary: The traditional bronze cougar statues are temporarily outside the RAD Center.
cards.evidence_claim: UH says the iconic cougar statues are temporarily outside the RAD Center during Centennial Plaza construction, and documents the paw-rubbing tradition.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor location; the temporary placement is associated with Centennial Plaza construction.

cards.title: Set out something red for Friday
cards.subtitle: Ninth stop: join a weekly campus tradition
cards.notes: Bring or wear a red item on Friday as a simple way to recognize a university-wide Cougar tradition during your first week.
cards.evidence_claim: UH declares every Friday Cougar Red Friday and encourages its campus community to wear red on Fridays.
cards.source_title: History and Traditions | University of Houston
cards.access_notes: No special access is required; this is a voluntary tradition.

cards.title: Check the Weeks of Welcome calendar
cards.subtitle: Tenth stop: choose one student event
cards.notes: Use the official schedule to select an event that fits your interests, location, and access needs; schedules and offerings change each year.
cards.short_summary: An official welcome-period calendar for connecting with campus programs.
cards.evidence_claim: UH states that Weeks of Welcome events are free and open to all UH students.
cards.source_title: Weeks of Welcome | University of Houston
cards.access_notes: Dates, locations, and accommodation information are published on the official event schedule; verify the current calendar.
